speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) has been monitoring the developments in different sectors of our economy, to guard against anti-competitive behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In the case of third party food delivery companies, they have explained publicly that their commission rates are in line with those charged before the start of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: During the Circuit Breaker period, some of these companies have offered assistance to restaurants and hawker stalls, such as removing on-boarding fees, waiving commission for self-collection orders and charging zero commission in the first month for businesses that are new to the platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Third party food delivery companies offer food ordering, delivery and payment services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: They are also aggregators that offer food services businesses access to their customer networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The food delivery companies have explained that their commission rates are required to cover their business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These include insurance and payment to their riders, as well as costs to develop and maintain the IT systems and databases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There are vendors who can help food services businesses to set up their own online storefront, with co-funding support from Enterprise Singapore (ESG).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There are also ground-up initiatives to help food establishments publicise their products and reach out to consumers directly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: One example is the "Hawkers United – Dabao 2020".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is a group that was formed on social media to help hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In addition, food services businesses can choose how the food reaches consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This includes self-collection by consumers, delivery by the food services businesses themselves, and using the services of third party logistics providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Some food outlets offer a combination of these options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There are trade-offs among the different options, and market conditions will also evolve in tandem with changes in supply and demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Third party food delivery companies may charge higher commission rates, but they can offer end-to-end services and access to a larger consumer base.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Hence, food services businesses should weigh the pros and cons of the different options before making a commercial decision on which one they want to choose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This approach will produce a better outcome for all stakeholders compared to capping commission rates through legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The availability of alternative options, including the possibility of new competitors entering the market, will serve as a check against excessive commission rates and continue to incentivise delivery companies to provide value to businesses who are using their platforms and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government will continue to support our companies and our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Our objective is to help viable businesses to survive this crisis and to prepare for the recovery, when we are able to gradually ease the restrictions and allow more economic activities to resume.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We have various schemes in place to help our companies and workers, covering different areas such as workforce training, productivity improvement and adoption of digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Our businesses who need assistance can approach Enterprise Singapore and the Trade Associations and Chambers and we will do our best to help them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The objective is to reduce the costs for food services businesses which are using these online platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For food services businesses that choose to go through approved third party logistics partners to deliver meals to their customers, ESG will assist them by co-funding 20% of the delivery cost that they are paying to these third party logistics providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It was originally scheduled to end on 4 May.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: They have a dominant share and continue to have a dominant share during this COVID-19 period and there has been a lot of feedback from F&B outlets whether help can be given to them.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What I would like to ask Senior Parliamentary Secretary is whether the Government has monitored the size and growth rate of the delivery platform business, especially since the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Whether the Government feels legislation should be necessary to govern the practice of such businesses – I would say they are very large now – to avoid predatory behaviour as well as provide transparency, some kind of format that they have to provide transparency to the consumers to show how much the delivery companies charge restaurants and pay the delivery riders.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I think that form of transparency is important.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The same practice has been imposed on banks.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: If we do not do a permanent arrangement, can we do a temporary one, so as to provide these restaurants a fighting chance to survive?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And there are many other cities in the process of doing so.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Speaker, Sir, when we assess the policy options, I think it is important that we look at the incentives that these policies will create and the outcomes that they are likely to produce and not only on the intent of the proposal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we may have good intent when we suggest certain policy changes using legislation, but it does not mean that good intent alone will produce positive outcomes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is something which we have to be quite careful in deciding what option we want to take to tackle the problem.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In my main reply, Sir, I mentioned that an effective way of dealing with this issue is to create alternative options so that you give businesses and consumers choice.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is a check against anyone – whether it is GrabFood, foodpanda, Deliveroo or any other company – being able to charge excessive commission rates.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is what we have been trying to do.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To reduce the entry barrier to help companies that want to seek out alternative options.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These options can include having customers pick up their own food.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It can include the food services companies working with a third party provider to deliver the food on their behalf.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And what rate do you want to set?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If you set it too low, one of the consequences would be that the food delivery companies would then not be able to provide some of these services because they have their costs to cover as well.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And they have explained what cost component goes to who – how much of it goes to the riders, how much of it for insurance, supporting the IT systems and maintaining the customer databases.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, yes, I think we do need to keep an eye on making sure that the system is fair, making sure that there are sufficient alternative options.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But in the end, I think we should place our focus on what is the outcome that we can achieve.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Actually, I would like to speak by apologising to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I had mentioned "Senior Parliamentary Secretary"; it is actually "Senior Minister of State".

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I have made my point, so I will not repeat myself.
